result.description: Customer messaging and support platform (inbox, help center, AI agent Fin) with a public REST API for contacts, conversations, tickets, articles and more.
result.auth_detail: Access Token (bearer) for private apps on your own workspace; OAuth2 required for public apps accessing other workspaces. Both sent as Authorization: Bearer.
result.access_detail: Private app: access token from Developer Hub, no review. Public/multi-tenant app (what Composio would need): free US-only development workspace, OAuth setup, Intercom review before publishing. Dev workspaces free but limited. Docs state no paid-plan requirement for API. Custom OAuth redirect URIs for MCP need support allowlisting.
result.api_notes: REST at https://api.intercom.io, versioned via Intercom-Version header (e.g. 2.11, plus preview). Covers contacts, conversations, companies, articles, tickets, etc. (breadth from general knowledge; docs pages fetched only showed Contacts example). Official SDKs exist.
result.blocker: Public OAuth app needs Intercom review before other customers can connect; dev workspace is US-only. Private token path is self-serve.

evidence.quote: To access the Intercom API, you have two authentication options depending on whether you app is public or private.
An Access Token is issued to the teammate who installed the app on the workspace, or who last regenerated the token.
Development workspaces are free and intended for development purposes only.
You can build a private app using your Access Token and it does not require a review.
Development workspaces are only available for the US region.
The Intercom MCP server is available for US and EU hosted workspaces.
The Intercom MCP Server provides 16 tools for interacting with the Intercom API.
